rules.title: HTTPS, modern TLS, secure transport
rules.what: Serve over HTTPS with modern TLS versions; redirect http to https; no obsolete protocols (SSLv3, TLS 1.0/1.1).
rules.why: Security is the non-negotiable floor (NR-SERVICE-004 note): an obsolete protocol is both a vulnerability and a slower handshake on every connection.
rules.how: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers, HSTS where appropriate, certificates monitored for expiry; broken links and mixed-content resources fixed.

verify.how: sslscan/sslyze output shows supported protocols within policy; no mixed content warnings.

limits: Never trade this rule for any performance or sobriety gain.

rules.title: Containers sized to what runs
rules.what: Container images contain only what the process runs: multi-stage builds, no build tools in the runtime image, slim base, no unnecessary layers.
rules.why: Fat images tax every pull, every deploy and every registry: transfer time, storage, cold starts. Build tools in a runtime image are dead weight that also widens the attack surface.
rules.how: Multi-stage Dockerfiles, distroless or slim bases, .dockerignore complete, pinned digest dependencies, image size tracked in CI.

patterns.note: Full distro base; slim/alpine variants usually suffice for the runtime stage.
Build toolchain installed; verify it is not in the final stage.

verify.how: Image size in CI under the stated budget; history shows build tools only in build stages.

limits: Debugging sometimes needs a fuller image; make it an explicit tool, not the default.

rules.title: Region and locality decisions on evidence
rules.what: Choose hosting regions and data locality from latency, data-protection constraints and, where relevant, the electricity mix - and cite the source of any environmental claim.
rules.why: Region choice moves latency (retries, timeouts), data transfer cost and, where the provider publishes it, the carbon intensity of the compute. A choice this consequential deserves its evidence.
rules.how: For each region: latency to the audience, data-protection fit, provider-published carbon data (if used, cite the report and date). Do not invent mixes from memory.

verify.how: Region decision recorded with latency measurements and, if environmental, a citable provider report.

limits: Provider carbon data changes with the grid; an environmental claim carries its date and source.

rules.title: Deferrable work in low-impact windows
rules.what: Schedule deferrable batch work (backups, rebuilds, reindexes, training) in off-peak or low-carbon windows where the grid publishes such data.
rules.why: Work that waits a few hours can run when the grid is cleaner or the infrastructure is less contended - same work, lower marginal impact, no functionality change.
rules.how: Identify deferrable jobs, schedule them in the off-peak window with a stated source for the window (grid data, provider schedule), keep deadlines explicit.

verify.how: Job schedule documented with its window source; deadlines unaffected.

limits: Only applies to genuinely deferrable work; user-facing latency never waits for a grid.

rules.title: Clean environments and orphaned resources
rules.what: Environments, volumes, snapshots and load balancers are inventoried with owner and TTL; orphans are deleted, not ignored until the invoice arrives.
rules.why: Cloud waste is dominated by idle resources nobody remembers creating; they bill and power-consume 24/7 for zero user value.
rules.how: Tag everything with owner and expiry; scheduled audit of untagged or expired resources; preview environments auto-destroy.

verify.how: Cloud inventory shows owner and expiry on every resource; expired items removed within policy.

limits: Deletion of production data needs authority (NR-SERVICE-007).

rules.title: Extend hardware life
rules.what: Prefer extending the useful life of hardware (servers, devices) over replacing it: amortise longer, buy refurbished where it fits, retire on evidence of limits not fashion.
rules.why: Manufacturing dominates the lifecycle footprint of most digital equipment: keeping a device one more year avoids more impact than any usage optimisation on its successor.
rules.how: Refresh policies based on measured need (NR-SERVICE-004); refurbished for non-critical roles; component upgrades over full replacement where possible.

verify.how: Refresh/procurement policy references measured limits and amortisation.

limits: Security support end-of-life overrides life extension (NR-SERVICE-004 note).

rules.title: CI that spends what it must
rules.what: CI runs are incremental, cancelled when superseded, with bounded caches and artifacts; pipeline duration and cost are tracked.
rules.why: CI is a multiplier: every push times every job times every branch. Unbounded caches and un-cancelled redundant runs grow silently with the team.
rules.how: Cancel-in-progress on updated PRs, dependency caching bounded by size policy, only test what changed where the tooling allows, artifact retention short.

patterns.note: Inverted check: absence of a concurrency block on PR workflows is the finding.

verify.how: Pipeline minutes and cache sizes tracked over time; redundant runs cancelled in practice.

limits: Some jobs (nightly full builds) are deliberate; the rule targets waste, not scheduled work.

rules.title: Scalability without waste
rules.what: Scale horizontally on demand with a floor sized to reality: autoscaling floors and ceilings measured, not guessed; scale-to-zero where the cold start is acceptable.
rules.why: A fixed fleet sized for the peak burns the peak cost around the clock; pure scale-to-zero adds cold-start latency to every request. The measured floor and ceiling beat both extremes.
rules.how: Set autoscaling bounds from observed load percentiles, alert on ceiling proximity, evaluate scale-to-zero only where the latency budget tolerates the cold start.

verify.how: Autoscaling bounds traceable to observed percentiles; utilisation and cold-start metrics reviewed.

rules.title: Interruptible capacity only for interruptible work
rules.what: Use spot or preemptible capacity only for workloads that checkpoint safely, tolerate interruption and do not expose personal data through requeued work.
rules.why: Spare capacity is cheaper and uses otherwise idle hardware, but interruption, retries and migration have their own cost; on the wrong workload they cancel the saving.
rules.how: Checkpoint at bounded intervals; idempotent tasks; compare retry and migration overhead with the expected saving.

verify.how: Interruption drill: the job resumes from its checkpoint without duplicated work or data exposure.

rules.title: Choose hosting on evidence
rules.what: Choose a host and region from published, verifiable data (energy source, PUE, water, hardware lifetime) and the service's real needs, not from labels.
rules.why: Hosting accounts for a large share of a service's footprint; claims without data cannot be compared and often do not hold.
rules.how: Request the provider's measured indicators; prefer providers publishing methodology; record the choice and its sources.

verify.how: Hosting decision record lists the indicators and their sources.

rules.title: Edge execution only when it pays
rules.what: Run at the edge only when the reduced transfer or latency offsets replication, invalidation and deployment overhead; document residency and consistency.
rules.why: Replicating code and data to many locations multiplies storage, deployments and invalidations; the gain exists only for the traffic that needs it.
rules.how: Measure latency and bytes saved per request against the added replication; keep personal data out of shared edge caches without review.

verify.how: Before/after latency and transfer on real traffic; residency documented.

rules.title: IoT and embedded: budget sampling, radio and sleep
rules.what: Define sampling frequency, payload size, sleep cycle and update budget for devices; batch telemetry with bounded local storage; test worst-case memory and energy on target hardware.
rules.why: Every sample and transmission wakes the radio and drains the battery; frequent firmware pushes and chatty telemetry multiply that across the fleet.
rules.how: Increase fidelity only when the decision it serves is demonstrated; batch and compress telemetry; define loss, retry and deduplication before raising frequency.

verify.how: Energy and memory measured on the target device for the worst-case cycle.
